faq: What kind of rules can you check?

Sums that must match, dates in sensible ranges, amounts over limits, required fields, values that must exist in your own list, and duplicates. You tell us the rules, and we also suggest ones we commonly see.
Does this prove my data is 100 percent correct?
No. Checks catch many errors but not all, which is why we add a sample audit in the Premium package. Important items should still be reviewed by a person.
Can you add checks to a flow someone else built?
Often yes, as long as we can see where the data goes and get collaborator access. We review the flow first and confirm in writing what we can add.
Who decides what to do with flagged items?
Your team. Flagged items go to a review list with the reason, and a person approves, fixes or rejects them. We do not auto-correct values unless you ask for a specific rule.

desc:
Accuracy checks and review flags for your data stop wrong values from reaching your books, stock counts or customers. Ecom Swift LLC adds rule-based checks to your existing data flow and sends every doubtful item to a review list with the reason attached.

## What are accuracy checks and review flags?

Accuracy checks are rules that test each processed record against what you already know must be true. A total must equal the sum of its lines. A due date cannot fall before the invoice date. An amount above an agreed limit needs a second pair of eyes. When a record breaks a rule, it is flagged with the reason and placed on a review list instead of moving on silently.

The checks sit after the reader or the typist, like a proofreader, and ask the same small set of questions about every record.

## Why unchecked data costs more than it seems

Automatic reading and manual typing both make occasional mistakes: a misread digit, a day and month swapped, a missing tax line, a supplier name spelled two ways. One wrong value rarely looks serious on its own. But it travels into a payment, a stock figure, a monthly report or a customer email, and by then it is hard to trace.

A checking layer moves the discovery to the earliest possible moment, when the record is still one line in a queue and the original document is a click away.

## How checks improve quality and save time

Checks give your team a reason to trust the records that pass. Without them, people re-read everything to be safe, which is slow and still misses things. With them, attention goes only to the flagged items, so review time is spent where a problem was actually detected.

The counts matter as well. When you can see how many records passed, failed or needed a person, patterns appear, and fixing the source is cheaper than catching the same error every week.

## What a good set of checks includes

- Arithmetic rules, such as line items adding up to the stated total and tax matching the rate you use.
- Date rules, such as no future invoice dates and no due date before the issue date.
- Required fields that must not be empty before a record is accepted.
- Range limits for amounts, quantities and discounts that your business rarely exceeds.
- Cross-checks against your own lists, such as approved suppliers, product codes or customer numbers.
- A reason message on every failure, written in plain words a colleague can act on.
- A review list with room to approve, correct or reject each flagged item.
- A tally of passed, failed and reviewed records so you can see how often a person is needed.

## How we build and test the checks

We start by reading a sample of your records and asking which mistakes have actually cost you something. You tell us the rules in your own words, and we turn them into clear, testable checks. Nothing is added that you have not approved.

Next we run the rules against real records from your files and look at every failure together. Some will be genuine errors, others will show that a rule is too strict, and we adjust until the flags are useful rather than noisy. The Basic package covers one data flow with a core set of rules. Standard adds cross-checks against your lists, a review queue and alerts for repeated failures. Premium extends the work across several flows with a scorecard, a sample audit of items that passed and a rule guide so your team can edit rules later.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start with the mistakes that have cost you money or time, not every possible rule.
- Write a reason on every flag so reviewers know what to look at.
- Decide in advance who reviews flagged items and how quickly.
- Revisit the rules when your suppliers, products or forms change.
- Keep the original document linked to each flagged record.

**Avoid:**
- Adding so many rules that every record is flagged and reviewers stop reading.
- Setting limits that are never checked against real, recent examples.
- Treating a passed record as proven correct, since a check only catches what it was written to catch.
- Letting flagged items pile up without an owner.
- Changing a rule without testing it on past records first.

## Who this service is for

It suits a bookkeeper whose invoice reader occasionally misreads totals and who cannot afford to post a wrong bill. It suits an online seller importing supplier price lists, where one bad column can change hundreds of prices. It also suits an office team that already extracts data from forms or documents and now wants evidence of how often a person is still needed.

## What we need from you

Send a sample of recent records, including a few that you know were wrong, and a short list of the rules you would apply if you had time to check by hand. We also need to know where the data lives and who will handle the review list. We never need your passwords. Where a tool supports it, you give us access as a collaborator, team member or developer user, so the work stays in your own account.
